title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy of Music on 1972-03-25
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> Samplitude Professional v11.2.1 -> FLAC/
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: Historic show with a unique Bo Diddley opener and strong highlights like “How Sweet It Is” and “Deal”, captured on a now‑pristine soundboard recording
ai_review.review: The concert is notable for its rare first‑set collaboration with Bo Diddley and Donna Jean’s early vocal debut, delivering standout moments such as a smoking “How Sweet It Is”, an urgent “Sittin’ on Top of the World” and a fiery “Deal”. The restored SBD source sounds clean and balanced, though a few reviewers note occasional buzzes; overall the performance is energetic with some second‑set dips (e.g., “Playin'”).

ai_rating.rationale: Average user rating is 4.0, reviewers praise historic musical moments and a clean soundboard source while noting a few weak second‑set songs, yielding a solid above‑average combined score

recording_quality.technical_notes: After recent restoration the SBD is described as ‘perfect shape’, crisp and clear; occasional minor buzzes noted but overall very listenable

standout_songs: Sittin' on Top of the World
show_quality.setlist_flow: Unique Bo Diddley opening set followed by two Dead sets; historic first set with Donna’s debut and rare covers, second set mixes strong jams with a few less‑focused numbers

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s noodling on “B.E. Women” praised; noted for bending notes and fiery soloing especially on “Deal” and “Sittin' on Top of the World”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Strong, urgent bass lines highlighted throughout; vocal contributions on “Last Train” and “Brown Eyed Women”.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s harp work praised (“Smokestack”, “Bertha”), with mentions of his energy driving jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Possible theremin/pedal‑steel texture noted; Keith’s playing mentioned in relation to Pigpen boogie‑woogie sections.
